style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The first of the church's seven penitential psalms, and the rawest: there is no confession of a specific sin in it, only a man so sick and so afraid of God's anger that the two have become one thing. Rebuke me not in Your anger; be gracious, for I am wilting; heal me, for my bones are in panic and my soul is terrified -- and You, O LORD, how long? The argument he makes is the argument of Psalm 30 and of Hezekiah: in death there is no remembering You; who thanks You from the grave? Save me, then, for Your covenant love's sake, and keep a voice in the choir. Verses 6 and 7 are the Bible's most vivid picture of a sleepless grief -- every night the bed swims, the couch dissolves in tears, and the eye wastes and ages from vexation. Then, without any recorded answer, the turn: get away from me, all you workers of iniquity, for the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping. He has heard; He will receive. The enemies who were exalted will turn back ashamed, in an instant. Weeping, in this psalm, is a form of prayer God hears -- the tears had a voice.

1.text: For the choir director, with stringed instruments, on the eight-stringed lyre. A psalm of David. O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger; do not discipline me in Your burning wrath.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] on Neginoth [neginah] upon Sheminith ['upon the eight', sheminith, the KJV margin], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. O LORD [YHWH], rebuke [yakach] me not in Your anger [aph], neither chasten [yasar -- discipline] me in Your hot displeasure [chemah -- heat, fury].
1.notes: The first penitential psalm opens without denying the rebuke -- only its temperature: al-be-appekha tokhicheni (H639, H3198), not in Your anger; al-ba-chamatekha teyassereni (H2534, H3256), not in Your heat discipline me. David accepts yasar, fatherly correction (cf. Proverbs 3:11-12); he begs off chemah, the fury. Psalm 38:1 repeats the line almost word for word.

2.text: Be gracious to me, O LORD, for I am wilting away; heal me, O LORD, for my bones are shaking in terror.
2.amp: Have mercy [chanan -- be gracious] upon me, O LORD [YHWH]; for I am weak [umlal -- languishing, withered]: O LORD, heal [rapha] me; for my bones [etsem] are vexed [bahal -- terrified, thrown into panic].
2.notes: umlal ani (H536): I am wilted -- the word for a drooping plant. rephaeni YHWH (H7495): heal me -- the illness is literal, and the bones (atsamai, H6106) nibhalu (H926), are in panic -- the Aramaic twin of this bahal is the word for Belshazzar's terror at the writing on the wall (Daniel 5:6, 9). Terror down to the skeleton.

3.text: My soul, too, is utterly shaken with terror -- and You, O LORD: how long?
3.amp: My soul [nephesh] is also sore [meod] vexed [bahal -- terrified]: but You, O LORD [YHWH], how long?
3.notes: nibhalah meod (H926, H3966): the bones' panic has reached the nephesh (H5315). Then the sentence that breaks off: ve-attah YHWH -- ad-matai -- 'and You, LORD -- how long?' The Hebrew has no verb; the question is left unfinished, the way a sob is.

4.text: Turn back, O LORD; pull my soul free; save me for the sake of Your covenant love.
4.amp: Return [shub], O LORD [YHWH], deliver [chalats -- draw out] my soul [nephesh]: oh save [yasha] me for Your mercies' [chesed -- covenant love] sake.
4.notes: shubah YHWH (H7725): turn back -- God has turned away, and David asks Him to turn around. chaltsah naphshi (H2502, H5315), draw my soul out -- the verb used of drawing a sandal off a foot (Deuteronomy 25:9); hoshieni (H3467) le-maan chasdekha (H2617): the only warrant he offers is God's own covenant love -- no merit is on the table in a penitential psalm.

5.text: For in death there is no remembering You; in the grave, who will give You thanks?
5.amp: For in death [mavet] there is no remembrance [zeker] of You: in the grave [sheol] who shall give You thanks [yadah]?
5.notes: The argument of Psalm 30:9 and Hezekiah's sickbed (cf. Isaiah 38:18): ki en ba-mavet zikhrekha (H4194, H2143) -- in death no one is remembering You -- bi-sheol mi yodeh-lakh (H7585, H3034). Not a denial of the afterlife but a claim on this one: a living worshiper is worth keeping alive. God is asked to protect His own praise.

6.text: I am worn out with my groaning; every night I make my bed swim; I dissolve my couch with my tears.
6.amp: I am weary [yaga] with my groaning [anachah -- sighing]; all the night ['every night', layil, the KJV margin] make I my bed [mittah] to swim [sachah]; I water [masah -- melt, dissolve] my couch [eres] with my tears [dimah].
6.notes: The Bible's most vivid insomnia: yagati be-anchati (H3021, H585), exhausted by my own sighing; be-khol-lailah ascheh mittati (H3915, H7811, H4296) -- I make my bed SWIM, sachah being the swimming-verb; be-dimati arsi amseh (H1832, H6210, H4529), I melt my couch. Hyperbole, and every grieving person knows it is not.

7.text: My eye is worn out from grief; it has aged because of all my adversaries.
7.amp: Mine eye [ayin] is consumed [ashesh -- wasted, moth-eaten] because of grief [kaas -- vexation]; it waxes old [athaq -- grows old] because of all mine enemies [tsarar -- those who press me].
7.notes: asheshah mi-kaas eni (H6244, H3708, H5869): the eye eaten away -- the word is kin to the moth -- by kaas, the vexation Job's friends misread. atheqah be-khol-tsorerai (H6275, H6887): the eye AGED by the adversaries; grief as premature old age. Verse 7 is the only place the enemies enter before the turn.

8.text: Get away from me, all you workers of iniquity, for the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.
8.amp: Depart [sur] from me, all ye workers [paal] of iniquity [aven]; for the LORD [YHWH] has heard [shama] the voice [qol] of my weeping [bechi].
8.notes: The turn, with no recorded answer in between: suru mimmenni (H5493), get away from me, kol-poale aven (H6466, H205) -- Jesus quotes the line to the false disciples of Matthew 7:23. The reason: ki-shama YHWH qol bikhyi (H8085, H6963, H1065) -- the LORD has heard the VOICE of my WEEPING. Tears, in this psalm, have a voice God can make out.

9.text: The LORD has heard my plea for grace; the LORD will receive my prayer.
9.amp: The LORD [YHWH] has heard [shama] my supplication [techinnah -- plea for grace]; the LORD will receive [laqach -- take up, accept] my prayer [tephillah].
9.notes: shama YHWH techinnati (H8085, H8467): the plea for grace HAS been heard -- perfect tense, settled -- and YHWH tephillati yiqqach (H8605, H3947): the prayer will be taken up, received like an offering. Between verses 7 and 8 nothing visible changed; faith's tense changed.

10.text: Let all my enemies be put to shame and utterly shaken with terror; they will turn back and be shamed -- in an instant.
10.amp: Let all mine enemies [oyeb] be ashamed [bosh] and sore [meod] vexed [bahal -- terrified]: let them return [shub] and be ashamed [bosh] suddenly [rega -- in a moment].
10.notes: The panic changes sides: yevoshu ve-yibbahalu meod kol-oyevai (H954, H926, H3966, H341) -- the same bahal that shook David's bones (v. 2) and soul (v. 3) is handed to the enemies. yashuvu (H7725), they turn back, as David asked God to turn back (v. 4); and rega (H7281), suddenly -- Psalm 30:5's 'moment' of anger, now the moment of their undoing.
